note: The game calendar: a simplified lunisolar Jewish calendar. It is a deterministic gameplay approximation, NOT a reconstruction of first-century practice. Days run sunset to sunset and are counted from Day 1; the seven-day week never resets. See docs/calendar.md.

months.note: Nisan-based religious-year order. In a leap year the year ends with two months named below instead of 'Adar'.

lunation.note: Month lengths (29 or 30 days) come from a fixed mean lunation, so every playthrough agrees. The real months began when the new moon was first seen, which no formula reproduces.

intercalation.note: Leap-year policy. 'metonic' repeats a 19-year pattern (a later computational convenience, not the first-century rule); 'never' makes every year ordinary. 'overrides' maps a year number to true (leap) or false (ordinary) and always wins.

start_date.note: The protagonist game opening: 1 Kislev, Year 1, 07:00. A simulated gameplay anchor, not an asserted historical date, and NOT the baptism date. The baptism happens on whatever date the player reaches the Jordan trigger; that date is recorded from the playthrough (CanonicalTimeline.trigger_baptism).

anchors.note: Story dates fixed in data, looked up by Calendar.anchor_day. There is deliberately no baptism anchor: the baptism is ministry Day 0 and its calendar date is recorded when the player triggers it. Festivals stay on their fixed calendar dates (festivals.json) whatever date that is.
